title: Wireless (C9800)
description: The C9800 WLCs from model-driven telemetry (Prometheus job wlc, wlc_* series): controllers, APs and radios, channel use and RF, SSIDs and clients.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Clients in RUN state on the selected WLCs (client-live-stats).

panels.title: APs joined
panels.description: APs whose CAPWAP state is registered (capwap-data, sent every 60 s). An AP that leaves just stops reporting, so it drops out of the count.

panels.title: Radios up / total
panels.description: All AP radios joined to the selected WLCs (ewlc-ap-stats).

panels.title: Radios down
panels.description: Radios that are joined but not up: admin down or, like the C9130's second 5 GHz (XOR) radio here, not in use.

panels.title: Telemetry age
panels.description: Seconds since Prometheus last scraped each WLC's CPU sample (pushed every 30 s, scraped every 30 s, so normally under 30). Telegraf keeps serving a sample for 150 s after the last push, so a broken dial-out reads 150 s and more, then counts up (see the Monitoring stack dashboard, journalctl -u telegraf on the backend VIP holder, and the WlcTelemetryNotInPrometheus alert).

targets.expr: time() - max by (host) (timestamp(wlc_cpu_five_seconds{host=~"${wlc:regex}"})) or time() - max by (host) (max_over_time(timestamp(wlc_cpu_five_seconds{host=~"${wlc:regex}"})[$__range:30s]))

panels.title: WLC SNMP
panels.description: Prometheus' SNMP scrape of the WLCs (job snmp-wlc).

panels.title: Controllers
panels.description: Per WLC, now. Linux CPU is the mean busy % over the control-plane cores; IOSd CPU the 1-minute figure of the IOS daemon alone (usually near 0 on a C9800-CL). Click a WLC for its log lines.

targets.expr: topk by (host) (1, max by (host, high_availability_state, memory_stats_memory_status) (wlc_control_process_info{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}))

panels.title: Linux CPU busy per core
panels.description: 100 - idle for each control-plane core (per-core-stat, a 5 s sample every 30 s).

panels.title: Linux memory used
panels.description: Control-plane Linux memory (the WLC's warning and critical thresholds are 88 % and 93 %).

panels.title: IOSd CPU and load
panels.description: IOS daemon CPU (1-minute %) and the Linux 1-minute load average.

panels.title: Access points
panels.description: Every AP joined to the selected WLCs, now (capwap-data every 60 s). Clients = associated clients over the AP's radios. Last disconnect is the reason of the AP's previous CAPWAP drop. Click an AP for its join/leave lines in the network device logs. Uptime counts from the AP's boot, Joined for from its CAPWAP join; Certificate expiry is the AP's manufacturing (SUDI) certificate. Known gap: the WLC's telemetry drops the first entry of each list; extra per-entry subscriptions restore the 2.4 GHz radio and the lowest WLAN, but the client with the lowest MAC and the 2.4 GHz noise/interference scan stay missing; see wireless.py.

targets.expr: topk by (host, wtp_mac) (1, max by (host, wtp_mac, name, wtp_ip, device_detail_static_info_ap_models_model, device_detail_static_info_board_data_wtp_serial_num, device_detail_wtp_version_sw_version, ap_state_ap_operation_state, ap_mode_data_wtp_mode, tag_info_site_tag_site_tag_name, tag_info_policy_tag_info_policy_tag_name, tag_info_rf_tag_rf_tag_name, disconnect_detail_disconnect_reason) (wlc_ap_capwap_info{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}))
topk by (host, wtp_mac) (1, max by (host, wtp_mac, oper_status) (wlc_ap_ethernet_info{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}))

defaults.noValue: No APs joined to the selected WLCs

panels.title: Radios
panels.description: Every AP radio, now. Channel is the primary channel (Channels: the bonded set). Tx power level 1 is the radio's maximum. Channel busy (CCA) is the share of time the radio heard the channel busy: its own transmit, receive from its clients and everything else; RRM measures it every 180 s. Tx/rx are the radio's own traffic over the last 6 minutes (the AP refreshes these counters every 180 s). Known gap: the WLC's telemetry drops the first entry of each list; extra per-entry subscriptions restore the 2.4 GHz radio and the lowest WLAN, but the client with the lowest MAC and the 2.4 GHz noise/interference scan stay missing; see wireless.py.

(max by (host, wtp_mac, radio_slot_id) (wlc_ap_radio_band_phy_tx_pwr_lvl_cfg_cfg_data_curr_tx_power_in_dbm{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}) or max by (host, wtp_mac, radio_slot_id) (wlc_ap_radio_radio_band_info_phy_tx_pwr_lvl_cfg_cfg_data_curr_tx_power_in_dbm{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}))

(max by (host, wtp_mac, radio_slot_id) (wlc_ap_radio_band_phy_tx_pwr_cfg_cfg_data_current_tx_power_level{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}) or max by (host, wtp_mac, radio_slot_id) (wlc_ap_radio_radio_band_info_phy_tx_pwr_cfg_cfg_data_current_tx_power_level{host=~"${wlc:regex}"}))
